title: Unit – 4 : Session – 1 : SLO – 2  |  Functional vs Imperative Paradigms
sections: A pure functional approach is better for adding two numbers because the operation is a pure function: given the same two inputs it always returns the same result, with no dependence on — and no modification of — any external state.
Predictability: add(2, 3) is always 5, regardless of when or how many times it is called, whereas an imperative version may read or mutate global variables, so results can change with program state.
Testability: pure functions need no setup or mocks — they can be unit-tested in isolation.
Referential transparency: any call can be replaced by its result, enabling safe refactoring, caching (memoization) and parallelism.
No side effects: the calculator's other features can never be accidentally corrupted by the addition logic, which is a real risk with imperative state mutation.
